# Clarity

When in doubt, choose the simpler word, the more obvious affordance, and the
more conventional layout. Cleverness shifts comprehension cost onto the user;
clarity respects their time.

## Examples

- "Delete project" — clear about destination and scope
- "Are you sure?" — vague; what's the user about to do?
- A button labeled "Submit" without context — what is being submitted?

## When to break this rule

Almost never. If you find yourself reaching for clever copy, consider whether
the underlying flow is too complex.
